summary: Configured a DHCP relay chain so node3 (isolated on node1's eth2 segment) obtains its address from node2's DHCP service (isolated on node1's eth1 segment). Built out the missing segments (192.168.10.0/24 between node1↔node2, 192.168.20.0/24 between node1↔node2's DHCP-served node3 segment), installed and configured dnsmasq on node2 as the DHCP server for 192.168.20.0/24, installed and configured isc-dhcp-relay (dhcrelay) on node1 to relay broadcasts between eth1 and eth2, and added the return route on node2 (via node1) so DHCPOFFER/ACK unicast replies reach the relay's giaddr. All configuration was made persistent (static /etc/network/interfaces.d entries and sysctls on node1, static interface + boot route script on node2, dhcp-on-boot on node3), and verified across a full one-at-a-time restart of all three nodes with new boot IDs and automatic post-reboot recovery of the relay chain (node3 re-acquired lease 192.168.20.139 fully automatically after its own reboot).
actions_performed: Surveyed all three nodes' network topology, interfaces, and running services
Identified node1 (SONiC/Debian) has unconfigured eth1 (toward node2) and eth2 (toward node3), forming two separate L2 segments
Discovered node2 had no DHCP server (only dhcpcd client) and node3's eth1 was down/unconfigured
Installed isc-dhcp-relay on node1 via apt
Installed dnsmasq on node2 via apk
Enabled IPv4 forwarding globally and per-interface on node1
Configured dnsmasq on node2 with dhcp-range 192.168.20.100-200/24 and router option 192.168.20.254, bound to eth1
Configured and started isc-dhcp-relay on node1 relaying eth1<->eth2 to server 192.168.10.10
Diagnosed via tcpdump that DHCPDISCOVER/OFFER were exchanged between relay and server, but node2 lacked a return route to 192.168.20.0/24 for unicast replies to the relay's giaddr
Added route on node2 (192.168.20.0/24 via 192.168.10.254 dev eth1) fixing the reply path
Verified node3 obtains a full DHCP lease (192.168.20.138/139) via udhcpc and via persistent ifup/dhcpcd

Persisted all configuration: node1 static interfaces.d file + sysctl.d + systemctl enable isc-dhcp-relay; node2 static interfaces file + /etc/local.d boot route script + rc-update add dnsmasq/local; node3 auto eth1 dhcp in /etc/network/interfaces
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, service status, addressing, leases) on all three nodes

Restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time (systemctl reboot / reboot), polled each until exec was available again, confirmed changed boot_id each time, and verified relay/server/client recovery and a fresh end-to-end DHCP lease after each restart

evidence.requirement: node2's DHCP service and node3 are on different segments of node1, requiring a relay to bridge them
evidence.summary: Baseline topology showing node1 eth1 (facing node2) and eth2 (facing node3) as separate unconfigured segments, and node2/node3 each with a second down NIC (eth1)

evidence.requirement: DHCP server configured and running on node2 for node3's subnet
evidence.summary: dnsmasq started on node2 with dhcp-range for 192.168.20.0/24; log shows DHCPDISCOVER/DHCPOFFER exchanges for node3's MAC

evidence.requirement: DHCP relay agent configured and running on node1 between the two segments
evidence.summary: isc-dhcp-relay active with dhcrelay process bound to eth1 and eth2, forwarding to 192.168.10.10

evidence.requirement: Root-caused and fixed the missing reverse route so DHCP replies reach the relay from the server
evidence.summary: tcpdump proved DISCOVER reached relay/server but OFFER never returned to client; added route 192.168.20.0/24 via node1 on node2 to fix the return path

evidence.requirement: node3 successfully obtains its address from node2's DHCP service via the relay (end-to-end functional proof)
evidence.summary: udhcpc and persistent dhcpcd/ifup on node3 both successfully obtained lease 192.168.20.138/139 from server 192.168.10.10 through the relay

evidence.requirement: Configuration persists across reboot (not just runtime state)
evidence.summary: Static interfaces.d/sysctl.d files and systemctl enable on node1; rc-update add dnsmasq/local and boot route script on node2

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered relay service and networking
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 39fdb9ab..., reboot acknowledged, post-reboot boot_id changed to c14f1af9..., dhcrelay/sysctls/IPs auto-recovered, and node3 successfully re-leased through node1 afterward

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered DHCP service and data (leases)
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b7edc71d..., reboot, post-reboot boot_id changed to bee8f6f1..., dnsmasq/eth1 IP/route/lease-file all recovered, and end-to-end lease succeeded afterward

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered DHCP client lease automatically
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 407511a0..., reboot, post-reboot boot_id changed to 4fbaa74d..., and node3 automatically re-acquired its 192.168.20.139 lease via dhcpcd on boot with no manual steps
